title: The alias table leaves the gitignored corpus directory (R1007 slice 2)
body:
Slice 2 of `docs/plans/oracle/tracked-alias-table.md` — **OD-11 / R1007**, evidence **BL-4**. Completes R1007.

`git mv data/aliases.toml aliases.toml`, contents byte-identical. `DEFAULT_ALIAS_TABLE` and `config.toml` follow it in the same commit, because R1007 requires the file and its config default to move together. A fresh clone now carries the table; nothing is force-added.

**`.gitignore` is not edited, and that is the point.** The table was kept in git by `git add -f`, not by a negation rule, so the exception retires by becoming unnecessary. `data/` stays ignored (R21).

**New: `tests/test_alias_table_location.py`** — the ratchet. Nothing else in the suite would notice the table falling back out of git, because every other alias test writes its own table into `tmp_path`; that blindness is the defect BL-4 filed. It asserts the default path resolves to a real parsable file, that git tracks it, that git does not ignore it, and that it is not under the corpus directory.

The ignore assertion is paired with `data/` as a **negative control**: `check-ignore` also exits non-zero when the ignore machinery is not working at all, so without the pair a missing `.gitignore` would make the test green. It skips with a stated reason where git is absent or this is not a work tree (R20), so the suite stays green from an unpacked source archive.

`tests/test_config.py`'s two default assertions flip from `data/aliases.toml` to `aliases.toml`. That is the assertion this slice exists to change; nothing is weakened and the defaults-agree test is untouched.

5 new tests, 486 passing. Offline throughout — the git calls are subprocesses in the checkout, not network.

Carries a merge of the base branch so the required checks run against the tree this will land on.
